We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 6 reactions, using templates in order: ['20810', '2895', '1914397', '1914398', '1914399', '74054'].

We have applied first three templates, got products (precursors). Need to continue applying remaining templates to each appropriate precursor to eventually reach simple building blocks.

We need to construct a tree JSON where each reaction node uses given template_id (as integer? example uses number). Provide children as precursor molecules (type mol). For each reaction, we need to apply template to the target molecule (the parent). The order must be as given, meaning first reaction uses template 20810 to break target into two precursors. Then each of those precursors may be further broken using next template? Usually sequential: apply 20810 to target, then apply 2895 to one of the resulting precursors (maybe the larger fragment), then 1914397 to one of those, etc. Need at least 6 reactions total, using all six templates in order. So we need a linear chain of 6 reactions, each step applying next template to the previous product (the target of that step). That means each reaction's product is the precursor from previous step? Actually retrosynthesis: start from target, apply template to get precursors. Then pick one of those precursors as new target for next step, apply next template, etc. So we need a path of depth 6.

We have after template 20810: precursors: "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1" and "O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1F". Choose one to continue. Likely the larger fragment will be further broken with 2895 etc. So we continue with the first precursor.

After 2895 applied to that precursor, we got "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1". So we continue with that.

After 1914397 applied, we got two precursors: "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCNCC1" and "O=[N+]([O-])c1cc(Br)c2c(c1)CCC1(CCC1)O2". Choose one to continue with next template 1914398.

Probably continue with the aromatic brominated fragment "O=[N+]([O-])c1cc(Br)c2c(c1)CCC1(CCC1)O2". Apply template 1914398 to that.

Let's apply.
